text.font-family: 'Pinyon Script', 'Great Vibes', 'Monsieur La Doulaise', 'Brush Script MT', cursive

g.text: Vecino

svg.text: One community word, fine-line, no explanation

g.text: FRONT
DISEÑADO EN SALT LAKE COUNTY
BACK
LETTERING AT PRINT SIZE, 13 IN WIDE
Why this word
Vecino: neighbor. It is what the West Side calls itself and what
Comunidades Unidas and Centro Civico say in their own copy. It belongs
to every nationality here: Mexican, Venezuelan, Salvadoran, Peruvian.
Nobody owns it as a brand. Paisa is Paisa Boys' name. Raza is contested.
Hyna is Born x Raised's. Familia and Barrio are on a thousand tees.
Vecino is a plain statement with a second meaning for the visitor:
you are a neighbor here too, if you act like one.
The hand
Mister Cartoon fine-line: a single-weight 0.5 pt line, no fills, script
capitals, a tail that becomes the underline. Pinyon Script stands in here.
A Salt Lake letterer redraws it by hand (ink on vellum, scanned, vectorized).
Women's cut carries VECINA: same drawing, one letter, same hand.
Print test: 230 mesh, white water-based ink, one pass.
If the line fills in, go up a mesh, not a line weight.
SPEC
Blank: boxy heavyweight tee, drop shoulder, 1 in rib collar, tubular body. Unisex plus a women's cut (VECINA).
Fabric: 7.5 oz (255 gsm) 100% ringspun cotton, garment-dyed black, enzyme washed so the line sits on a soft surface.
Decoration: front, one-color white water-based screen print, 13 in wide x 5 in tall, centered 3 in below collar; back neck 801 1.25 in wide; hem line 4 in wide.
Colorway: Ink #212121 body, white ink. Second run: Forest #0D4C26 body with Cream #F6F1EC ink. Neck label: salt-crystal line icon plus partner-org line.
